messages:
jane-cs: FYI customer on mobile hit a weird partial stream + duplicate billing on reconnect, opened a ticket. repro steps included.

michael-customer: saw stream stop mid-sentence, then app reconnected and the first ~20 tokens came again, and we got charged twice for same output. i can share headers/logs.

jane-cs: thanks @michael-customer. can you paste the client SDK version and the exact reconnect behavior? is it closing then opening a new SSE, or reusing the socket?

michael-customer: mobile network flapped -> client closes and reinstantiates SSE. no idempotency header set. happens every ~30s when flaky.

alex-engineering: possible cause: client opens a fresh request w/o resume token or request-id so server treats it as a new generation and we stream prefix tokens again. we should check server-side dedupe window.

tara-support: asking for trace id + X-Request-Id from the failing session so we can look at logs. michael, can you share the request headers from the first and the reconnect attempt?

michael-customer: headers pasted:

```
GET /v1/stream?model=... HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Sdk-Version: mobile-1.3.7
User-Agent: MobileClient/1.3.7
X-Client-Request-Id: 0a7f3c
```

then reconnect shows: `X-Client-Request-Id: 1b9d2e` (different).

alex-engineering: yep different request id -> new server generation. also saw our billing event emitted on stream close and again on the new generation start in logs.

tim-sre-bot: Log snippet for trace 2026-08-09T12:11:23Z:
```
[12:11:23] session-start req=0a7f3c user=michael
[12:11:26] stream-abort req=0a7f3c reason=client-disconnect
[12:11:27] charge-event req=0a7f3c tokens=38
[12:11:28] session-start req=1b9d2e user=michael
[12:11:29] generation-chunk req=1b9d2e tokens=20 prefix="<same-first-20-tokens>"
[12:11:30] charge-event req=1b9d2e tokens=38
```

jane-cs: that log makes it clear. customer wants a recommended workaround and a timeline for a permanent fix.

alex-engineering: temporary workaround: client should attach a stable `X-Client-Request-Id` (or `idempotency-key`) that survives reconnects for the same logical request. server currently dedupes within a request-id window. If you set the same id, the server will detect duplicate start and attempt resume semantics instead of starting a fresh generation.

tara-support: share this minimal reconnect snippet with them (JS-ish) — client stores lastSeq and requestId and reattaches on reconnect:

```
const id = savedRequestId || uuid();
const es = new EventSource(`/v1/stream?model=...&request_id=${id}`);
es.onmessage = (e) => {
  // parse seq and skip tokens <= lastSeq
  const obj = JSON.parse(e.data);
  if (obj.seq <= lastSeq) return; // dedupe on client
  lastSeq = obj.seq;
  handleChunk(obj);
};
// on reconnect re-use same request_id
```

michael-customer: can the server help more? reusing ids and client-side seq checks are doable but brittle across app restarts.

alex-engineering: long-term fix: we should expand our resume protocol so server emits a resume token on first connect and accepts `X-Resume-Token` on reconnect, mapping to the same generation and streaming only the remaining tokens. Also add server-side idempotency over a longer window for identical request payloads. I can spin up a PR for the resume header + SSE comment: `: resume-token=...`.

jane-cs: customers will like a short-term recommended SDK change + config. please propose exact header names and a small changelog note.

alex-engineering: propose:
- client to send `X-Redwood-Request-Id` for logical request id (short-term)
- server to accept `X-Redwood-Resume-Token` on reconnect (future)
- server to include `: resume-token=<token>` SSE comment on first event
- server to include `seq` for each chunk and `final=true` on final chunk

I'll open an internal RFC and PR.

tara-support: suggested message to customer:
"We recommend shipping a small client change: persist a single request id for the duration of the logical generation and re-use it across reconnects. As a defence-in-depth, check `seq` values and ignore duplicates. We have a server-side fix planned to return resume tokens to make this robust; ETA T-shirt size: 2 sprint cycle. We'll escalate billing refund if duplicates caused incorrect charges in the interim." :thumbsup:

michael-customer: that's fine. i'll implement the request-id change and client seq guard today and report back. appreciate the fast triage.

alex-engineering: thanks, @michael-customer — please include one failing trace if it occurs again and we'll pick it up. I'll drop the RFC link when created.

tim-sre-bot: Incident note appended to ticket 78910: duplicate-charge risk for SSE reconnects when request-id changes.

jane-cs: closing loop here after customer confirms. will post follow-up after they ship mobile fix.
